Schema: # One line per table. Columns are separated by SEMICOLONS, because the
# WhereClause and KeyColumns fields contain commas of their own.
# Lines starting with # are ignored, so you can work through a large database
# in batches by commenting tables in and out.
# Generate these lines automatically with 01_discover_and_config.sql - it
# fills in the date column and the key for you. The examples below are from
# my own test database, so replace them with your own.
#   WhereClause   Which rows to take from the OLD server.
#                 Empty means the whole table.
#                 Do not use double quote characters in here - single quotes
#                 around dates and text, as in SQL.
#   KeyColumns    How to recognise a row we already have. Prefer a real
#                 business value over the automatic ID where you have one.
#   KeepIdentity  1 = keep the original ID numbers (normal)
#                 0 = let the new server allocate fresh ones (only for the
#                     tables that 02_check_gap_and_collisions.sql flags)
